Reconciliation now matches on the verbatim address string as C does, including the DNS consequence: an unchanged string whose resolution moved does not rebind. Deliberately different in ordering -- every NEW address is bound BEFORE any removed one is closed, where C frees first and can end with zero listeners and sudo_fatalx. A reload that cannot bind therefore changes nothing here instead of exiting the daemon; the cost is that swapping two listeners' ports needs two reloads. Guarded by TestReload_RebindsListeners and TestReload_UnbindableAddressKeepsPreviousListeners.

tls_ciphers_v12 selects TLS 1.2 suites by IANA name, not as an OpenSSL cipher string -- nothing in Go can parse 'HIGH:!aNULL', so a config written for C fails to load rather than being guessed at. Only the forward-secret AEAD suites in tls.CipherSuites() are selectable; tls.InsecureCipherSuites() is never consulted, so no config can negotiate CBC or 3DES. An unknown name fails the load where C warns and silently reverts to its defaults, which would leave a typo'd hardening change appearing to be in effect. No tls_ciphers_v13 counterpart: Go ignores CipherSuites for TLS 1.3 entirely. C's v13 default (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384) is among the three Go offers, so the default path negotiates the same suite.

Configurable now, with C's semantics: the first configured pattern replaces the default set rather than adding to it, patterns over 1024 bytes are rejected, and any compile failure aborts the config load. Deliberately different in the DEFAULT set: C ships one pattern ([Pp]assword[: ]*) and this ships nine covering en/de/es/fr/pt/ru/CJK prompts plus PIN and passphrase. The divergence only ever masks more than C, never less. Go's regexp handles a leading (?i) natively, so C's convention for requesting case-insensitivity is accepted as written.

log_format accepts sudo (the default, matching C's field order and octal control-character escaping) and json. Deliberately different for json: this emits one compact object per line, where C's json is currently an alias for json_pretty and rewrites the entire file as a single object on every event. That shape cannot be tailed, appended to by two writers, or shipped line-by-line, which is what an event stream is for. C's json_compact and json_pretty spellings are not accepted.

facility is implemented with C's table and case-sensitive matching, defaulting to authpriv. Deliberately absent: server_facility, the separate facility for the daemon's OWN warnings. Those go to slog here, which is configured by server_operational_log_level and its own handler, not by a syslog facility.

logfile.path is implemented, opened O_WRONLY|O_APPEND|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW as C does and flock'd per write. Deliberately different for time_format: this takes a Go reference-time layout rather than C's strftime string, because translating strftime would mean shipping a parser for a format nothing else in this config uses. C's default '%h %e %T' is 'Jan _2 15:04:05' here, and is the default.

The unlink condition now matches: a journal is removed only after the upstream's final commit_point for an I/O session, or after a fully transmitted event-only session, which C treats as complete because it sends no acknowledgement for those at all. Deliberately different for a journal that can NEVER be acknowledged -- an I/O session with no ExitMessage, from a client that died or a crash-truncated cache file. C leaves those to be retried on every daemon start; here they are renamed to *.incomplete, so the bytes survive for an operator and nothing replays them forever. Guarded by TestIOSessionWithoutExitIsParkedNotRemoved.

This requirement documents a C behavior rather than a contract: a journal the upstream answers with an error stays in outgoing/ and is retried on every subsequent start, forever, with no poison-message or dead-letter handling. Deliberately NOT reproduced. An error or abort ServerMessage is a definitive refusal -- the upstream parsed the session and said no -- and is now distinguished from a failure to be reached: the journal is renamed to *.rejected, which matches neither orphan-recovery glob, and the retry loop ends. Transient failures still retry forever, which is the store-and-forward behavior operators expect. Guarded by TestRejectedOrphanIsParkedNotRetried.
